title: His father's dance band and brother Tommy's Dixieland piano
summary: He describes the 1930s dance repertoire of his father and his self-taught older brother Tommy, who quit in the late 1950s because of rock and roll.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Alto. The tape machine is making a little scraping noise. Anyway, what kind of music did your father play? I never did quite understand about that.

Yeah, he played in what you would call fast-forward style a little, that kind of music. They had trumpet, saxophone, piano, bandwagon, bass I guess was a drum. They played like, you know, all these songs from the 30s, Evergreen, all this stuff. It's not really a jazz band, it was more a dance band. But he knew most of the tunes that I used to play too.
And your brother, what kind of music did he play?
He was a Dixlam piano player. He was self-thought. He never took any lessons.
And is he older than you then?

Yeah, yeah. He's 27 I think now. Yeah, 26, 27. But he just quit playing. He's married for a couple of years ago. He quit playing quite early by the way. He quit playing sometime in the late 50s because he didn't like that everybody liked rock and roll music. He figured there was no use of playing no more.
